author: Mark Atwood
text:
Deferred pending production-backend consumer demand. The bead itself explicitly says 'MemoryBackend doesn't notice (HashMap reads are cheap), but a production SQL-backed implementation processing a 100-emoji destroy batch issues 100 round-trips today vs 1 batched.'

The kit has no SQL-backed reference impl today; the only consumer of the per-entry pre-fetch is the in-memory backend where the cost is negligible. Implementing the batched pre-fetch adds ~50 lines of code and new tests for the batched path, against no measurable benefit today.

Re-open when a SQL-backed CustomEmoji consumer (stoa, kith, or third-party) reports the N-round-trip latency in real workloads.

The same N→1 batched-pre-fetch optimization applies to several other handlers (Space/set update gate, Message/set reaction-author check, etc.); a future workspace-wide perf-tuning epic should sweep them together rather than this bead in isolation.
